## Claim record — posted retroactively, and the reason it is late is a failure of mine

- **Session**: `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o` (`domain:engine` PM seat, seat post #6367)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-11991-emission-identity-source`
- **Dispatched**: 2026-08-26 ~12:30Z. This record: ~13:56Z, **after** the work landed as PR #12591.

I assigned this card and then posted the claim comment **to the wrong issue** — the text went to #5499 in the same turn. So from dispatch until now, #11991 carried an assignee and no evidence of which session held it.

That is not a bookkeeping nicety. All agents in this repo share one GitHub identity, which is exactly why a claim is defined as **assign *plus* a comment carrying the session ID and branch**: the assignee field cannot tell another seat whose claim it is. The prescribed check against double-dispatch is "re-read the comments before writing code" — and any seat that ran it on this card would have found only the triage note, and would have been entitled to take the card and duplicate the work.

The dev seat holding it noticed the card claimed a comment existed, verified none did, searched for a competing session ID, found none, proceeded, and **reported the gap in its return** rather than quietly assuming. That is the behaviour that contained this; the containment was theirs, not mine.

Recorded in §7 of the seat post. No competing claim was ever present, and nothing was duplicated.
